text: {"question":"What new evidence regarding the Hubble tension was highlighted at the recent conference, and how does it compare to earlier discussions of early- and late-universe models for resolving the tension?","reference_answer":"The conference emphasized that the Hubble tension remains at about 5σ, with no resolution yet, and presented DESI data suggesting a time‑varying dark‑energy equation of state peaking near redshift 0.5, a new late‑time effect not previously emphasized in early‑universe models such as early dark energy or dark radiation.","passage_1_contribution":"Passage A outlines early‑universe proposals (EDE, dark radiation) and late‑universe models (phantom‑like dark energy, chameleon dark energy) but notes unresolved debates and no‑go arguments.","passage_2_contribution":"Passage B reports that the Hubble tension persists at ~5σ and introduces DESI evidence for a sharply peaked dark‑energy density at z≈0.5, indicating a new late‑time modification.","joint_reason":"Both passages address the same scientific issue—the Hubble tension—and show an evolution from theoretical model proposals to new observational evidence for a late‑time dark‑energy feature.","same_quantity":true}
